saw_lines: Cyclists buy shoes once, fit them to their feet, then replace them only when the old pair wears out.
So the sale is won or lost in line one, where the offer and price settle the doubt before the click.
Your site offers 25% off an accessory, yet 0 of 15 ads mention percent off, so put the 25% off in line one of three new ads and on the creative.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 12 Oct 2026
points: Your site offers 25% off an accessory, yet 0 of 15 ads mention percent off, so a first time buyer has no reason to act. Put the 25% off in line one of three new ads and on the creative.

Your site shows prices from $49.99 to $529.99, yet 0 of 30 ads mention price. A buyer needs a number before clicking, or the ad gets skipped. Lead one ad with the $179.99 price and name the tier it compares to.

Your site explains how orders arrive, yet 0 of 30 ads cover delivery. Someone buying shoes online wants the timing settled before clicking. Show the box arriving in one video ad and put the delivery window in the first line.

None of your 30 ads shows a proof number, so new buyers have nothing concrete before the click. Pick one real figure you can stand behind, such as a review count or orders shipped, and open the next batch with it.
